newsitem.title: DUBAI: German politician had message from officials-Iran.
newsitem.headline: German politician had message from officials-Iran.

text.p: Iran said on Thursday that German politician Juergen Moellemann conveyed a message from top German officials during a recent visit to Tehran, at odds with Bonn over a court ruling that Iran ordered political killings.

"The spokesman for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, Mahmoud Mohammadi, said that the member of the German parliament and former finance minister, Jurgen Moellemann, in his recent visit to Tehran conveyed issues from top German officials for Iranian officials," the Islamic republic's state news agency IRNA said.
IRNA, in its report headlined "Foreign ministry spokesman says Moellemann conveyed message to Iranian officials", did not elaborate or give any further details.
The German Foreign Ministry had said Moelleman, who is regarded in Bonn as something of a maverick, had not been on a ministry assignment but had gone to Tehran last weekend on his own initiative.

"Mohammadi added that during the visit, planned by the German side, Moellemann held talks with relevant officials as a follow-up to technical negotiations held previously with the industrial establishments of the country," IRNA added.

An Iranian newspaper had said Moellemann during his two-day visit called for the restoration of bilateral diplomatic and economic ties between Germany and Iran, severed following the Berlin court ruling in April.

European Union states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after the court ruled that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of Kurdish dissidents in Germany. Iran has repeatedly denied involvement.
While the EU later agreed that the ambassadors could return to Tehran, the bloc has suspended ministerial ties as well as its "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Iranian officials have said the German ambassador would not be welcomed back in Tehran for the time being.

A German Foreign Ministry spokesman in Bonn said this week Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel had recently made it clear it was up to Tehran to make the first move by showing Bonn that the German ambassador to Tehran was welcome to return.
He said Kinkel had been cautiously optimistic about an improvement in relations after the new Iranian president Mohammad Khatami comes to power in August. "It is Tehran's turn now," he said.
